questions.q: Which opening is a report: 'The inter-school debate was held on 5 September at the auditorium' or 'The morning air buzzed with excitement as we entered the hall'?
questions.a: The first — it front-loads the 4W facts; the second is narrative scene-setting. A wrong answer reveals the student can't yet separate the report contract (inform first) from the story contract (immerse first).

questions.q: 'I really enjoyed the amazing science exhibition, it was the best day ever!!!' — fix for a report.
questions.a: 'The exhibition drew over 500 visitors, according to the organisers' — factual, third-person, quantified. A wrong answer that merely removes exclamation marks keeps first-person enthusiasm — the fix is changing the reporting stance, not the punctuation.

questions.q: Where does 'said the Principal' belong: 'The event was a great success, said the Principal' — correct quote integration?
questions.a: Yes — quote with attribution tag is standard. A wrong answer rewriting to 'the Principal was very happy' shows the student paraphrases away the attribution structure that reports use to certify factuality.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: A report records an event for readers who weren't there: ______ → byline → place+date → body in inverted pyramid (what happened → key details → quotes → outcome).

Fill in the blank: The inverted pyramid IS the genre: first ______ answers What-When-Where in one breath; the middle adds the how and a quote; the tail carries the least-critical detail — so an editor can cut from the bottom.
What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student structures a report in inverted-pyramid order, maintains past-tense third-person objectivity, integrates one quote correctly, and distinguishes report register from narrative register (no suspense, no 'I was so excited').

questions.q: Fill in the blank: Compare a report opening vs a story opening: 'The annual science exhibition was held on ______ March in the main hall' vs 'It was a bright morning when…' — same event, different contract with the reader.
